bestExpectedTarget.text: "I recall the days of our life together, When we were bound in wedded harmony. I was moved by how deep your love ran, And laughed that my fate held nothing but hardship. Too soon we parted, letting go each other's hands, And at the long pavilion you pressed wine on me again and again. Sorrow lingered on the mountain passes, And endless wind and dust kept us apart. We kept our vow across a thousand leagues, And looked toward each other under the half-moon. Six aimless years slipped quickly by, And I grieved as both my parents withered and fell. Some dawns I lay down to sleep on Hoanh Mountain, Some days I walked singing by the ford of the Dien(7). Climbing the tower, I wept the tears of Wang Can(8). Hunting for verses, I wore Duling's kerchief. Bamboo and stone could hardly cure my coarse ways, And with lute and wine cup I took no heed of being poor. In a strange land I strained my eyes in vain, While my homeland weighed on my wounded spirit. A wastrel's life was never my true calling, Yet staying away so long has worn this body down. Who could have known the guest of Penglai Isle Would send word from afar to her neighbor by the Brocade River? At Caishi I turned my oar back once more, At Huanggu I asked the way to the ford a second time. For years I dreamed of the Wu Gorge(10), Then in one morning came the spring of Wuling. Like butterflies we took up our old affection, Like mandarin ducks we found it fresh again. Lightly adorned, like the Lady of Guo in Tang, Lovely as the girl next door in Song. The green grows dense and the orioles' song turns rough. The red grows sparse and the swallows fret. In gallant roving, I am a Du Mu(11) of today. In this wondrous meeting, I am a Liu Chen of old. I chant my verses as the mood takes me. In romance, would I give way to any man? So fine a tale deserves to be handed down, So I take up the brush to record this wedded bond."

bestExpectedTarget.text: Alas, my lady! In womanly bearing, a model to all, In goodness and virtue, perfect and whole. Your spirit was graceful and serene, Your manner lovely and bright. When you came to be my bride, As husband and wife we were close and dear. Who could have known that midway on our path We would so suddenly be parted? My father took office in a distant land, And I went with him to serve. More than six years went by Without a word by goose or carp. Your spring chamber lay cold behind its curtains. The crane lamented, the gibbon grieved. Alas, the road you traveled, How hard and lonely it must have been! At the edge of the sky, at the corner of the sea, A traveler lay alone upon his mat. Then tidings from home came of a sudden, And I lashed my horse to hasten back. Once more the zither and the lute played in sweet accord, Once more the phoenix glue mended the broken strings. Scarcely had we rejoiced in our reunion When in an instant we were torn apart. How faithless I have been! How pitiable your fate! What more is there to say Now that it has come to this? Blossoms drift before the courtyard, The cassia falls from the midst of heaven. The hibiscus droops and withers, The willows hang tattered and torn. The scenery remains as it was, But you have wandered far away. With what shall I deliver your soul? With offerings at the temple. With what shall I console you? With a bond renewed in lives to come. Though mountains wear away and seas run dry, This sorrow shall never be eased. Alas, my lady, Deign to partake of this offering.

allowedTargetPoems.text: East of the imperial city, grass and trees grow thick and wild, A few ruined rooms stand at the bend of Khuc Giang. With silver comb and emerald tint, I tend my morning toilette, And in my misty chamber, by cloud-veiled windows, I pine alone. Since the age of sixteen I have guarded my fragrant beauty, And never let the butterfly envoys or bee matchmakers through. All day long I keep company with the red apricots on the bank, Glimpsing spring, yet too shy to turn toward the crowd of youths. Whose son is this young lord who comes with books beneath his arm, So broad in learning, so rich in talent, so versed in classics and histories? In one hasty glance across the top of the wall, My heart gave its pledge before any match was sanctioned. So I planted this humble flower to face the sun, And bade the Lord of Spring let it bloom in all its glory. The catkins greet the wind awhile, their fragrance forlorn, Their shadows, first touched by warmth, linger amid the tender green. Dew drips on the lush blossom, and its crimson heart unfurls, Dispelling all the bitter sorrows of springs gone by. In song I sway with the supple waist of Xiaoman (10), With rouge and powder I beguile you with a bosom like Xi Shi's (11). Counting on my fingers since we met, the stars have not yet come full circle, Yet mountains and rivers fill your eyes, and the wanderer wakes from his dream. Tears fall upon the letter the fish has carried from your native village, And my soul melts away as your horse takes the road to the plum-blossom post station. At the long pavilion the carriage wheels rumble at dawn once more, Bringing me, sick with grief, to pour your parting cup beside the road. In the western garden the yellow plums weep beneath the darkening rain, At the southern shore the green grass grieves above the cold waves. Yellow plums and green grass quietly wound the spirit; I remain while you go home, and our shadows part awhile. With all solemnity I sing this song for you, For at the hour of parting, one heart must surely break.

allowedTargetPoems.text: What do I love? Sleep, and sleep alone, For in sleep the heart finds ease and nature rests content. Lightly inked curtains add new wealth and honor; A winding rattan couch ties bonds of old affinity. Verandas of plum, gardens of bamboo— In secluded dwelling lies the joy of woods and springs. The green servant behind me, the red companion before me (5), Each time they lead me to the land of sweet dark slumber, my thoughts float light as air. With both hands I cover my ears against the red dust of the world; Bending my arm for a pillow, I lie in a white-thatched hut beside the clouds. Proudly lodging in a thatched cottage, idling through days and months at Nanyang (6); Stretching my limbs in a cloud-wreathed abbey, deeming the realm of Zhao Song too narrow (7). By the northern window, the poet's soul is easily stirred; In the western hall, spring dreams are ever whole (8). In the book tower, the sleeping mat is newly rolled away; At the wine shop, the sky is just clearing after rain. Night after night, the black crane of Huangzhou; Year after year, the fair one of the Xiang River (9) (10). At times I turn toward the land of drunkenness and lie down to sleep, With grass for my mat, flowers for my curtains, and the earth for my felt rug. At Pengze, deep in the night, half the blind holds the waning moon (11); In the quiet courtyard of Lianxi, a single pillow hears the cuckoo's cry (12). Let others call me what they will: a lazy good-for-nothing, a sleep-starved fellow, or a hidden immortal!

definitions.eligibleUnits: Unique exact-span prepared context units; structural headings/original-title spans and standalone Roman controls excluded. Equal text at different offsets counts separately.
definitions.pairedUnits: Entire original UTF16 unit span contained in the union of active non-lexical groups.parts[locale]. Alias-only groups never count as unit pairs; groups without parts do not contribute.
definitions.eligibleWords: Unique exact spans from artifact.editions[locale].words containing a Unicode letter and wholly within ONE eligible context unit. No word lookup calls are made.
definitions.anyRawLinkWords: Eligible words overlapping the union of raw source-side link spans from all active groups, including lexical aliases; no confidence threshold. Partial/unlinked partition uses raw overlap.
definitions.fullLetterWords: Every Unicode letter/mark UTF16 code unit inside an eligible word is covered by raw link-span union. Spaces/punctuation ignored; combining marks included; astral letters count two UTF16 units.
definitions.unitPercentageDenominator: eligibleUnits; paired unit percent is source pairing coverage, not semantic accuracy.
definitions.wordPercentageDenominator: eligibleWords; full/partial/unlinked are disjoint and sum to eligibleWords. Raw punctuation-only overlap is partial and recorded by linkedButNoLetterWords.
definitions.uiStrictMatchPct: 100*uiStatuses.match/uiQueriedUnits. Only full original unit quotes<=2000 UTF16 units are queried; errors and stale/pending/missing remain in denominator and never pass.
definitions.uiHighlightStatusPct: 100*(match+uncertain)/uiQueriedUnits; this is UI status coverage, not word confidence or correctness.
definitions.uiContextStatusPct: 100*(match+uncertain+context-only)/uiQueriedUnits; this includes context-only answers and is not strict matching.
definitions.exclusions: uiTooLongUnits are listed separately, excluded only from UI query denominators. Input and artifact source revision/version/hash/text/breaks must agree, and all40 source files are rehashed after reporting.
definitions.limitation: Entirely automatic structural/link inventory and full-unit UI statuses. These percentages are NOT semantic accuracy, translation quality, or a manual every-word review.
